    },
    {

  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:4902377507",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "whether collectTxs() can return missing transaction positions directly to reduce an IPC round trip",
      "quote": "This could be collapsed to the response \"JDS calls TxCollection::collectTxs() (this PR) with that Wtxid list\" to reduce the round trip?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained collectTxs is a constructor returning an interface and pipelining can chain requests",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4902958777"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:4928438822",
        "c:4962003449"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4902958777",
      "status_by_quote": "collectTxs() is the constructor so it needs to return an interface. I don't think it can return both the TxCollection interface and the list of missing transactions."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3544794067",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "order-dependent addition in addMissingTxs could leave partially applied state if an invalid transaction aborts the loop early",
      "quote": "AddMissingTxs is order-dependent, a bad entry aborts the loop at that point, so [valid, invalid] keeps valid but [invalid, valid] doesn't. Is this intentional? Correct me if I am wrong but validate-then-apply seems to be a safer approach.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "addressed in rebase",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5062080068"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5062080068",
      "status_by_quote": "Addressed @ViniciusCestarii's inline comments https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35671#pullrequestreview-4655098156"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3554795720",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "split into two Cap'n Proto interfaces (ExternalBlockTemplate and BlockTemplate) so disallowed methods fail at compile-time rather than throwing at runtime",
      "quote": "would it be worth splitting into two capnp interfaces instead of throwing on methods: an ExternalBlockTemplate with just getBlockHeader/getBlock/getCoinbaseMerklePath/submitSolution and BlockTemplate extends(ExternalBlockTemplate)",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "reviewer stated they are fine either way after author raised concerns about client duplication",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3640469762"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3640976129",
      "status_by_quote": "The split just removes what's currently unclear to a client consuming the interface (methods that appear callable but are guaranteed to throw). Just my two cents. I'm fine either way"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4974409738",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "non-differential indices allow repeated requests for the same transaction, risking buffer overflow or out-of-memory errors",
      "quote": "compact blocks uses a differential index not primarily for efficiency... but so that the wire format is safe by construction against an attack that applies the same large transaction over and over again (e.g. if index 5 is some giant txn, you request 5,5,5,5,5,5...) and overflows a buffer or OOMs an implementation explicitly constructs the block and without having to have expensive duplication checks.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained Mining IPC client trust model and local host assumption",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4978780547"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4978780547",
      "status_by_quote": "the Mining IPC client is expected to run on the same machine, so unknownTxPos() and addMissingTxs() are not designed for bandwidth efficiency. We also (currently) more or less trust the IPC client."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3642746508",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "check the size of wtxids before looping using MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT",
      "quote": "Should the size of `wtxids` be checked before the loop (e.g. perhaps using existing constants — `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT`)?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added the limit check in miner.cpp",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3644987599"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3644987599",
      "status_by_quote": "Added (similar check as in merkleblock.cpp), along with a test."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3642761322",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "avoid locking m_mutex in TxCollection constructor since the object is not yet shared",
      "quote": "nit: does the `m_mutex` need to be locked in the constructor? — the object isn't shared until after construction returns, so no concurrent access is possible yet.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author dropped the mutex lock in the constructor",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3644987886"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3644987886",
      "status_by_quote": "Dropped"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3765415437",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "check for duplicate wtxids in the constructor before locking the mempool",
      "quote": "I think the constructor could check for duplicates before locking the mempool? As the duplicate is entirely visible from the input.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added duplicate wtxid check prior to mempool lock",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820760263"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820760263",
      "status_by_quote": "Done, checking duplicates first without a lock now."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3765562606",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "call reserve on m_transactions before acquiring the mempool lock",
      "quote": "since the collection size is known, we could reserve it before acquiring the mempool lock to avoid the reallocating and rehashing while the mempool is locked",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented reserve prior to lock",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820760065"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820760065",
      "status_by_quote": "Done"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3766518873",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "add a test verifying that TxCollection retains transactions when they leave the mempool",
      "quote": "I think an improvement to this test would be adding a test to verify the mempool snapshot behavior. such that it tests that after the collection is constructed with a transaction in the mempool, if the transaction is removed from the mempool it does not report it as missing.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author incorporated suggested snapshot test",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820759831"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820759831",
      "status_by_quote": "Taken"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3767165227",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "document that all non-coinbase transactions must already be present in block.vtx before calling the coinbase helper",
      "quote": "The current documentation here does not mention that all the transactions must be present before calling this so that this does not happen.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added doc comment",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820759626"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820759626",
      "status_by_quote": "Taken."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3767376523",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "calculate height locally as a const in the coinbase helper instead of modifying BlockAssembler member",
      "quote": "I think a cleaner approach to this helper would be to have it calculate its own height... const int height{pIndexPrev.nHeight + 1}",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author adopted local calculation and made helper const",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820759345"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820759345",
      "status_by_quote": "Taken, and made it a const member function."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3768124604",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "limit m_mutex scope in MakeTemplate to checking completeness and copying transactions into a local vector",
      "quote": "Could we limit its scope to checking completeness and copying the ordered m_transactions into a local vector? The references remain valid after the lock is released, so block construction and TestBlockValidity would not need to hold the collection mutex.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author narrowed lock scope",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820759018"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820759018",
      "status_by_quote": "Done"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3768262990",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "why interruptWait is permitted on external templates when waitNext throws",
      "quote": "waitNext is disabled for external templates, but interruptWait is still allowed? Is there a reason for this?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author acknowledged oversight and disabled interruptWait as well",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820758849"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820758849",
      "status_by_quote": "Good catch, I probably missed this in a rebase (before I opened the PR)."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3768404613",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "addMissingTxs checks transaction count rather than weight, permitting oversized transaction payloads to be stored before block validation",
      "quote": "The check here is against the size, but it does not check the weight. So even though it can reject a million tiny transactions, it can accept 16666 large ones... This would be eventually rejected as oversized in makeTemplate when TestBlockValidity is called, but that is a bit too late.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined duplicating consensus checks done by TestBlockValidity",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3820690848"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3820690848",
      "status_by_quote": "I don't think we should take over too much work that TestBlockValidity() does for us. Duplicating consensus checks could introduce new bugs."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5125552680",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "why makeTemplate() uses stale-prevblk for ancestor prevhash when TestBlockValidity and checkBlock use inconclusive-not-best-prevblk",
      "quote": "makeTemplate() reports an ancestor prevhash as `stale-prevblk`, but `Mining::checkBlock()` reports that same case as `inconclusive-not-best-prevblk`... Was that difference deliberate?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author switched to inconclusive-not-best-prevblk",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5817134744"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5817134744",
      "status_by_quote": "Also addressed @jeanpablojp's feedback: switched to `inconclusive-not-best-prevblk`"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3944180465",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "add a test case for makeTemplate rejecting a coinbase with a mismatched witness commitment",
      "quote": "The amount case is covered, the witness commitment one isn't, and that's the one that pins which transactions the coinbase commits to. I flipped a bit of the commitment and it gives bad-witness-merkle-match. Would a case next to this one be worth it?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added test for mismatched witness commitment",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5817134744",
        "rc:4095390984"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4095390984",
      "status_by_quote": "Added such a test."
    }

participants.note: Concept ACK; asked about collapsing IPC steps to reduce round trips
raised concern on order-dependent addMissingTxs handling, suggested interface split, and demonstrated pipelining
noted non-differential indices risk buffer overflows or OOM; author explained IPC trust model
Concept ACK; suggested input size checking on wtxids and locking cleanup
Concept ACK; raised concern on lack of weight check in addMissingTxs; suggested locking and test improvements
Concept ACK after testing; asked about reject reasons and suggested test and documentation improvements

claims.text: whether collectTxs() can return missing transaction positions directly to reduce an IPC round trip
claims.quote: This could be collapsed to the response "JDS calls TxCollection::collectTxs() (this PR) with that Wtxid list" to reduce the round trip?
claims.status_note: author explained collectTxs is a constructor returning an interface and pipelining can chain requests
claims.status_by_quote: collectTxs() is the constructor so it needs to return an interface. I don't think it can return both the TxCollection interface and the list of missing transactions.

claims.text: order-dependent addition in addMissingTxs could leave partially applied state if an invalid transaction aborts the loop early
claims.quote: AddMissingTxs is order-dependent, a bad entry aborts the loop at that point, so [valid, invalid] keeps valid but [invalid, valid] doesn't. Is this intentional? Correct me if I am wrong but validate-then-apply seems to be a safer approach.

claims.text: split into two Cap'n Proto interfaces (ExternalBlockTemplate and BlockTemplate) so disallowed methods fail at compile-time rather than throwing at runtime
claims.quote: would it be worth splitting into two capnp interfaces instead of throwing on methods: an ExternalBlockTemplate with just getBlockHeader/getBlock/getCoinbaseMerklePath/submitSolution and BlockTemplate extends(ExternalBlockTemplate)
claims.status_note: reviewer stated they are fine either way after author raised concerns about client duplication
claims.status_by_quote: The split just removes what's currently unclear to a client consuming the interface (methods that appear callable but are guaranteed to throw). Just my two cents. I'm fine either way

claims.text: non-differential indices allow repeated requests for the same transaction, risking buffer overflow or out-of-memory errors
claims.quote: compact blocks uses a differential index not primarily for efficiency... but so that the wire format is safe by construction against an attack that applies the same large transaction over and over again (e.g. if index 5 is some giant txn, you request 5,5,5,5,5,5...) and overflows a buffer or OOMs an implementation explicitly constructs the block and without having to have expensive duplication checks.
claims.status_note: author explained Mining IPC client trust model and local host assumption
claims.status_by_quote: the Mining IPC client is expected to run on the same machine, so unknownTxPos() and addMissingTxs() are not designed for bandwidth efficiency. We also (currently) more or less trust the IPC client.

claims.text: check the size of wtxids before looping using MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT
claims.quote: Should the size of `wtxids` be checked before the loop (e.g. perhaps using existing constants — `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT`)?
claims.status_note: author added the limit check in miner.cpp
claims.status_by_quote: Added (similar check as in merkleblock.cpp), along with a test.

claims.text: avoid locking m_mutex in TxCollection constructor since the object is not yet shared
claims.quote: nit: does the `m_mutex` need to be locked in the constructor? — the object isn't shared until after construction returns, so no concurrent access is possible yet.
claims.status_note: author dropped the mutex lock in the constructor

claims.text: check for duplicate wtxids in the constructor before locking the mempool
claims.quote: I think the constructor could check for duplicates before locking the mempool? As the duplicate is entirely visible from the input.
claims.status_note: author added duplicate wtxid check prior to mempool lock
claims.status_by_quote: Done, checking duplicates first without a lock now.

claims.text: call reserve on m_transactions before acquiring the mempool lock
claims.quote: since the collection size is known, we could reserve it before acquiring the mempool lock to avoid the reallocating and rehashing while the mempool is locked
claims.status_note: author implemented reserve prior to lock

claims.text: add a test verifying that TxCollection retains transactions when they leave the mempool
claims.quote: I think an improvement to this test would be adding a test to verify the mempool snapshot behavior. such that it tests that after the collection is constructed with a transaction in the mempool, if the transaction is removed from the mempool it does not report it as missing.

claims.text: document that all non-coinbase transactions must already be present in block.vtx before calling the coinbase helper
claims.quote: The current documentation here does not mention that all the transactions must be present before calling this so that this does not happen.

claims.text: calculate height locally as a const in the coinbase helper instead of modifying BlockAssembler member
claims.quote: I think a cleaner approach to this helper would be to have it calculate its own height... const int height{pIndexPrev.nHeight + 1}
claims.status_note: author adopted local calculation and made helper const
claims.status_by_quote: Taken, and made it a const member function.

claims.text: limit m_mutex scope in MakeTemplate to checking completeness and copying transactions into a local vector
claims.quote: Could we limit its scope to checking completeness and copying the ordered m_transactions into a local vector? The references remain valid after the lock is released, so block construction and TestBlockValidity would not need to hold the collection mutex.

claims.text: why interruptWait is permitted on external templates when waitNext throws
claims.quote: waitNext is disabled for external templates, but interruptWait is still allowed? Is there a reason for this?
claims.status_note: author acknowledged oversight and disabled interruptWait as well
claims.status_by_quote: Good catch, I probably missed this in a rebase (before I opened the PR).

claims.text: addMissingTxs checks transaction count rather than weight, permitting oversized transaction payloads to be stored before block validation
claims.quote: The check here is against the size, but it does not check the weight. So even though it can reject a million tiny transactions, it can accept 16666 large ones... This would be eventually rejected as oversized in makeTemplate when TestBlockValidity is called, but that is a bit too late.
claims.status_note: author declined duplicating consensus checks done by TestBlockValidity
claims.status_by_quote: I don't think we should take over too much work that TestBlockValidity() does for us. Duplicating consensus checks could introduce new bugs.

claims.text: why makeTemplate() uses stale-prevblk for ancestor prevhash when TestBlockValidity and checkBlock use inconclusive-not-best-prevblk
claims.quote: makeTemplate() reports an ancestor prevhash as `stale-prevblk`, but `Mining::checkBlock()` reports that same case as `inconclusive-not-best-prevblk`... Was that difference deliberate?

claims.text: add a test case for makeTemplate rejecting a coinbase with a mismatched witness commitment
claims.quote: The amount case is covered, the witness commitment one isn't, and that's the one that pins which transactions the coinbase commits to. I flipped a bit of the commitment and it gives bad-witness-merkle-match. Would a case next to this one be worth it?
claims.status_note: author added test for mismatched witness commitment
